description: Issue #855 defect 3 (no unmutated baseline): run_mutant.py used to never run the declared red tests on a clean tree before applying the mutant patch, so it could not distinguish 'the mutant broke this test' from 'this test was already broken'. This fixture's declared red test is MutationGateSelftestFixtures.AlwaysFails_MutationGateBaselineSelftestFixture, which is permanently [Ignore]-d (see that class's doc comment) and therefore reports TRX outcome=NotExecuted -- never Passed -- both before AND after any patch is applied; the patch itself (a shared no-op, comment-only change to _FrameworkController.cs) is irrelevant to it. Before the fix: run_mutant.py applied the patch, built, ran the red filter, saw the (already-not-green) test fail to pass, found no red_expected_assertion_pattern on record for it, and reported UNEXPECTED_RED -- a FAILURE, but for the wrong diagnostic reason, and only by accident of the old evaluate_red() fallback for 'no pattern on record'; a mutant whose red test had SOME leftover pattern that happened to match a NotExecuted/blank message could have slipped through as KILLED with the old code, which is exactly the gap this defect describes. After the fix, evaluate_mutant() runs the red_test_filter on the CLEAN tree first (evaluate_baseline()) and rejects it deterministically as INVALID_MUTANT_BASELINE_NOT_GREEN before the patch is ever applied, regardless of what pattern is or isn't on record.
target_symbol: N/A -- the patch is a no-op (comment-only); this fixture exists to prove a red test that is not green on a clean tree is rejected as an invalid mutant, not to mutate real behaviour
